answer.rationale: The durable memory and archived sources show that promotional pricing (exp_73) drives short-term acquisition but fails at renewal, making it unsustainable under the primary objective of maximizing sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The competitor's price cut is triggering churn in price-sensitive SMB accounts—exactly the cohort least likely to retain. Rather than compete on price (which we know erodes cohort quality and retention), redirect focus to enterprise sales assistance (memory_44), which converts higher-value prospects through demo-request flows with superior pipeline quality. Simultaneously, leverage referral incentives (memory_57, exp_57) within established customers to generate qualified revenue without retention harm. This combination addresses the churn risk by shifting the revenue mix toward higher-quality, longer-duration accounts while protecting existing established customer relationships. A standard experiment allows measured rollout of enterprise sales assist positioning alongside referral activation in the base, avoiding the renewal-cycle cliff we observed in price-driven SMB acquisition.
